messages.content:
Outcome: Depressive symptoms (lower is better)

## Study A
Found: benefit
Claim: Depression scores on the HADs improved significantly more with vitamin D3 than with placebo in IBS-D patients.
Sentence: "Symptoms severity, QoL, HADs-depression, and VSI score improved significantly in the vitamin D group as compared to the placebo group (P-values: <0.001, 0.049, 0.023, and 0.008; respectively)."
Measured as: HADs-depression score
Population: Adults aged 18-65 with diarrhea-predominant irritable bowel syndrome
Intervention: Vitamin D3 50,000 IU/week for 9 weeks
Comparator: Placebo
Design: randomized controlled trial
Sample size: 74
baseline_vitamin_d_status: not_reported

## Study B
Found: no effect
Claim: Over 5 years, vitamin D supplementation versus placebo made no significant difference in change in depression scores among all participants.
Sentence: "There was no significant difference in change in the knee symptoms, depression, and serum levels of IL6 and hs-CRP between both comparisons after 3 years of cessation of the clinical trial."
Measured as: depression scores
Population: Adults with knee osteoarthritis from the Hobart centre of the VIDEO trial, followed up 3 years after 2-year treatment
Intervention: Vitamin D supplementation for 2 years, followed 3 years after cessation
Comparator: Placebo
Design: randomized controlled trial
Sample size: 173
baseline_vitamin_d_status: not_reported

content.text: {"rationale":"Both bear on vitamin D and depressive symptoms, but the two trials differ in population, dose and duration, and timing of assessment (end of 9-week treatment vs 3 years after a 2-year course ended), so the opposite results are genuine.","verdict":"genuine","reason":"population","also_differs":["intervention","outcome_measure"],"detail":"IBS-D adults, 50,000 IU/week for 9 weeks, HADs at end of treatment vs knee osteoarthritis adults, 2-year supplementation assessed 3 years after cessation"}
